observations: 1) REAL failure clip: From 00:00.000 to 00:02.000, the robot drives forward at night across a paved surface toward a white concrete barrier marked with a cone labeled '3'. Between 00:02.000 and 00:05.160, the robot pauses in front of the barrier (accelerometer az_g steady near 1.04g). At 00:05.260–00:09.000, it resumes driving straight into the barrier and cone instead of steering around it, colliding repeatedly (impact spikes at t=7.02s with ax_g=0.613g, ay_g=-0.945g, at t=8.02s with az_g=1.702g, and at t=11.20s with az_g=1.768g) before backing up slightly at 00:10.500–00:11.875.

2) OLD policy in the twin: From 00:00.000 to 00:00.750, the robot drives straight forward toward the large black cylindrical obstacle without steering away, colliding head-on around 00:00.625–00:00.750 and remaining pinned against the cylinder until 00:01.625.

3) NEW policy in the twin: From 00:00.000 to 00:00.750, the retrained policy exhibits nearly identical behavior to the old policy, driving straight into the black cylinder at 00:00.625–00:00.750 and staying stuck against it through 00:01.750. Across the 40 twin variants, success_rate remains 0.0, collision_rate barely changes from 0.90 to 0.875 (1 run shifting from collision to stall), and mean_peak_impact remains ~31.14.
